categoryName: Bakery — bread, buns, rusk, cake, biscuits, cookies

skuLines.examples: Britannia Sweet Slice / Milk Bread, Modern White, Harvest Gold Sandwich, Bonn White
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; term-time baseline, drops sharply in school/university vacation weeks
skuLines.notes: Shelf life only 2-5 days at ambient, less in heavy monsoon humidity. Needs inbound 2-3x/week minimum from Solan/Nahan/Paonta or a Ludhiana-based brand (Bonn) — this is the single hardest hill-logistics line. Store on open ventilated racks, never sealed cabinets; mould, not staling, is the loss driver at PIN 173101.

skuLines.examples: Britannia Brown, Modern Brown, Harvest Gold Brown, Bonn Brown
skuLines.notes: Same 2-5 day window as white. Buys mostly from staff households, not hostels; a smaller standing order than white.

skuLines.line: 100% whole wheat / atta bread, no maida
skuLines.examples: Britannia 100% Whole Wheat (No Maida), The Baker's Dozen Zero Maida Whole Wheat, English Oven 100% Atta
skuLines.notes: The health-led premium tier of bread; short shelf life, so keep facings low (1-2 SKUs) or it becomes the top expiry write-off in the category.

skuLines.examples: Britannia Multigrain, English Oven Multigrain, The Baker's Dozen Multigrain, Bonn Multigrain
skuLines.notes: Millet-added bread is the fastest-moving 2026 innovation slot in Indian bread. Two SKUs is enough; risk is the same short shelf life at a higher unit cost.

skuLines.examples: Britannia Milk Bread, Modern Milk Bread, Bonn Fruit Bread, local bakery sweet loaf
skuLines.notes: Sweet loaf eats plain, so it works for small children and for hostel rooms with no toaster. Higher sugar means slightly better mould resistance than plain white.

skuLines.line: Jumbo / institutional loaf (700-800g, sliced or unsliced)
skuLines.examples: Britannia 700-800g sandwich loaf, Harvest Gold jumbo, Bonn institutional pack
skuLines.notes: This is the canteen/warehouse SKU, not the POS SKU. Buy on a standing weekly indent against canteen menu, not on shelf-offtake — a 5,000-resident campus with two canteens is a bulk buyer, and the two flows should never be forecast from the same number.

skuLines.examples: English Oven Garlic Bread, Britannia Cheese-Chilli, local bakery masala loaf
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round, spikes around fests and hostel-night type events
skuLines.notes: Impulse-driven, short shelf life. Only worth carrying if the store can flush it in 48 hours — otherwise a guaranteed write-off.

skuLines.examples: The Baker's Dozen Country Sourdough, English Oven Classic Sourdough, The Baker's Dozen Fourgrain Sourdough
skuLines.notes: Sourdough is the No.1 talked-about bakery trend into 2026, but at ₹145-235 a loaf on a ₹208 average bill it is a 1-2 facing statement SKU for senior staff and visiting faculty, not a volume line. Fragile in transit over hill road.

skuLines.examples: Weikfield Bread Crumbs, Bonn Bread Crumbs, Tops Crumbs
skuLines.notes: Long shelf life (6-9 months) — the opposite risk profile to fresh bread, so it is a safe buffer SKU. Also the natural internal use for the store's own day-old bread if in-house baking ever starts.

skuLines.examples: Britannia Pav, Modern Pav, Harvest Gold Pav, local bakery pav
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; canteen pav-bhaji / chole-kulcha menu days drive spikes
skuLines.notes: 2-4 day shelf life. Highest hill-road-frequency dependency of any bakery SKU after sliced bread.

skuLines.examples: Britannia Burger Buns, English Oven Burger Buns, Bonn Buns
skuLines.notes: Ties directly to the canteens' burger/veg-patty menu — order against the canteen plan, not shelf history.

skuLines.examples: English Oven Sub Bread, Britannia Long Rolls, Modern Hot Dog Buns
skuLines.notes: Only if a canteen actually runs a sub/roll item. Otherwise this cannibalises burger buns and expires.

skuLines.examples: Modern Crem Treat Mango Cream Bun, Britannia Cream Bun, Bonn Cream Bun
skuLines.notes: One of the cheapest units in the whole bakery aisle on q-commerce (Modern Crem Treat is Blinkit's lowest-priced bakery item). At ₹15-25 it is a pocket-money price point — exactly the kind of SKU that lifts bills-per-resident rather than basket value.

skuLines.examples: Britannia Pizza Base, Modern Pizza Base, local bakery base
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; spikes on holidays and birthdays
skuLines.notes: Pulls cheese, sauce and veg with it — a basket-builder, not a standalone. 4-7 day shelf life, better than bread.

skuLines.examples: Britannia Toastea Premium Bake Elaichi Rusk, Priyagold Elaichi Rusk, Bonn Rusk, Anmol Rusk
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round, strong winter (Dec-Feb) peak with chai in a cold hill location
skuLines.notes: The single best line in this category for Baru Sahib: 4-6 month shelf life, no cold chain, travels fine on hill road, and it is the default chai accompaniment across every cohort from students to elderly. Stock deep and treat it as the monsoon buffer against bread stockouts.

skuLines.examples: Britannia Premium Bake Milk Rusk, Bonn Cake Rusk, Karachi/Amritsari cake rusk, Crispy Cake Rusk family pack
skuLines.notes: North-Indian cake rusk is a Punjab/HP habit, not a national one — expect it to over-index here versus any BigBasket/Blinkit national benchmark. Long shelf life, good margin.

skuLines.examples: Britannia Wheat Rusk, Priyagold Atta Rusk, Bonn Multigrain Rusk
skuLines.notes: The version elderly residents and diabetics ask for. One SKU covers it.

skuLines.line: Khari & fan (puff pastry), salty and sweet
skuLines.examples: Atul Bakery Khari, Madhur Khari & Fan, local Solan/Nahan bakery khari, Britannia Khari
skuLines.marginBand: 18-30% packed; 35-50% if bought loose and repacked
skuLines.notes: Loose-by-weight khari from a regional bakery is where the real margin is in this whole category — 3-5x the GM% of branded bread. Needs airtight jars/tins; goes soft fast in monsoon humidity.

skuLines.examples: Britannia Toastea bulk pouch, Bonn rusk institutional case, Anmol toast 1kg
skuLines.notes: For hostel/canteen tea service. Warehouse line, ordered on indent.

skuLines.examples: Britannia Orange Bites Slice Cake, Britannia Fruity Veg Cake, Winkies Slice Cake, Bonn Slice Cake
skuLines.notes: 6-9 month shelf life, no cold chain, ₹10-20 price point — the ideal SKU for a closed campus with 5,000 residents and 7.2 bills each per month. CRITICAL: stock EGGLESS/veg-marked variants only (Britannia's Veg/Fruity cake range); several packaged cakes and swiss rolls are explicitly 'contains egg' and are wrong for a Sikh institution's shelf.

skuLines.examples: Britannia Nut & Raisin Romance Slice Cake, Britannia Fruit Cake, Winkies Tea Cake
skuLines.notes: Eggless variants only. Long shelf life makes this the safe way to hold 'cake' on the shelf between fresh-cake orders.

skuLines.examples: Britannia Cup Cake, Winkies Muffin, The Baker's Dozen Choco Chip Muffin, Bonn Muffin
skuLines.notes: The practical substitute for a fresh cake when a hostel birthday needs something at 9 pm. Six-packs are the birthday format. Verify eggless on every SKU.

skuLines.examples: Winkies Chocolate Swiss Roll, Britannia Swiss Roll, Bonn Cream Roll, local bakery cream roll
skuLines.notes: Cream roll is a north-Indian bakery staple with a 3-7 day life if bought local; the packaged swiss roll keeps months. Winkies swiss roll is egg-based — check before listing.

skuLines.examples: The Baker's Dozen Brownie, Winkies Brownie, Britannia Treat Brownie
skuLines.notes: Premium impulse; needs a chiller or a cool shelf in summer or it goes greasy. Fits the university cohort and the Ary Lite counter better than the main POS store.

skuLines.examples: Britannia Festive Plum Cake 300g, Winkies Rich & Moist Plum Cake, Bonn Plum Cake
skuLines.seasonality: Sharp late-Nov to end-Dec peak — December alone is 25-35% of annual cake revenue for many Indian bakeries
skuLines.notes: Must be the alcohol-free / non-rum-soaked variant: this campus has no alcohol, and traditional plum cake is often rum-fed. Buy it once, in November, for a 6-week window; nothing left in January sells at full price.

skuLines.examples: Betty Crocker Eggless Vanilla, Pillsbury Cake Mix, Weikfield Cake Mix, Blue Bird
skuLines.notes: Real demand driver here is married staff quarters with small children and no cake shop within 30-50 km. 9-12 month shelf life, zero spoilage risk — a good margin/risk trade versus fresh cake.

skuLines.line: Fresh cream celebration cake — order-to-collect, eggless
skuLines.examples: in-house/canteen bakery 0.5kg & 1kg vanilla, chocolate truffle, black forest, pineapple; photo cake
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round, term-time; birthday volume tracks 5,000 residents ≈ 400+ birthdays a month
skuLines.notes: THE highest-margin line in the category and the biggest current leak: a resident who wants a birthday cake and cannot buy one on campus is a wallet leaving for a 30-50 km town trip. Requires a 2-8°C display chiller, an FSSAI manufacturing/kitchen endorsement if baked on campus, and an order-a-day-ahead book. 100% eggless is non-negotiable for a Kalgidhar Trust campus.

skuLines.examples: in-house pastry counter: chocolate, pineapple, black forest; regional bakery pastry (Krishna Bakery, Shimla style)
skuLines.notes: Needs a chiller and same-day disposal discipline; 24-48 hour life. Natural fit for the canteens and the F&V/Ary Lite counters, not for a warehouse indent.

skuLines.examples: regional bakery dry cake (Solan/Nahan/Paonta Sahib), Amritsari dry cake, Bonn dry cake
skuLines.notes: Ambient, 2-4 week shelf life, travels well on hill road, tea-time habit — a much better hill-logistics bet than fresh pastry, at similar margin.

skuLines.line: Loose bakery cookies by weight (jeera, atta, coconut, nankhatai, kaju, elaichi)
skuLines.examples: regional bakery jeera & atta biscuit, badam nankhatai, coconut cookies, Murthy's-style cheese biscuit
skuLines.notes: Bought loose from a regional baker and repacked in the store's own pouch, this is where a captive-market retailer actually makes money in bakery — versus 8-15% on MRP-locked branded biscuits. Needs airtight tins against monsoon humidity and a clean repacking/labelling practice under FSSAI.

skuLines.line: Savoury bakery — veg patties, puff, cheese roll
skuLines.examples: in-house/canteen veg patties, aloo puff, paneer puff; Shimla-bakery-style patties
skuLines.notes: Hot savoury bakery is the classic Himachal hill-town bakery footfall driver (Krishna Bakery, Shimla model). Same-day only; 100% vegetarian, no egg wash.

skuLines.examples: in-house glazed & choco doughnut, Winkies Donut, fresh cream bun
skuLines.notes: Only viable with in-house baking — 24 hour life, and no supplier 30-50 km away will deliver it fresh.

skuLines.examples: Parle-G, Britannia Tiger Glucose, Anmol Glucose, Sunder
skuLines.notes: Never a margin line — a traffic and credibility line. Running out of Parle-G in a closed township is a visible failure. 6-9 month shelf life, so over-stock it deliberately as monsoon buffer. Buy the 800g/1kg packs for hostel and staff-quarter households.

skuLines.examples: Britannia Marie Gold, Sunfeast Marie Light, Parle Marie, Anmol Marie
skuLines.notes: Also the default 'safe' biscuit for elderly residents and for babies past 12 months. High-rotation, no spoilage risk.

skuLines.examples: Parle Monaco, Sunfeast Snacky, Britannia Nutri Choice Cracker, Priyagold Classic Salted
skuLines.notes: Crackers & savoury biscuits are the largest single segment of the Indian biscuit market — do not under-space them relative to sweet biscuits.

skuLines.examples: Parle Krackjack, Britannia 50-50, Britannia Nice Time, Sunfeast Nice
skuLines.notes: Sunfeast Nice is among the cheapest average-price bakery brands on q-commerce — a genuine value slot for hostel students.

skuLines.line: Cream biscuits (bourbon, elaichi, orange, pineapple, strawberry)
skuLines.examples: Britannia Bourbon, Sunfeast Dream Cream, Parle Hide & Seek Cream, Anmol Cream Rolls, Priyagold
skuLines.notes: The highest-velocity sweet-biscuit block in a school/hostel population. Carry 5-8 flavours, not 2 — flavour variety is what drives repeat purchase in a captive market with nowhere else to go.

skuLines.examples: Britannia Good Day Butter & Cashew, Sunfeast Mom's Magic, Priyagold Butter Bite, Bonn cookies
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; family packs lift in winter
skuLines.notes: Good Day is a top-3 volume line in almost every Indian general store. Stock family packs for staff quarters.

skuLines.examples: Dukes Waffy, Britannia Treat Wafers, Priyagold Cheerio, Unibic wafers
skuLines.notes: Q-commerce shelves rusk and wafers together (Blinkit 'Rusks & Wafers'), so treat them as one buying block. Crushes easily in hill-road transit — order in outer cartons, not loose.

skuLines.examples: Parle-G ₹5, Monaco ₹10, Bourbon ₹10, Hide & Seek ₹10, Krackjack ₹5, Tiger ₹5
skuLines.notes: A deliberate buying decision separate from the pack sizes above. With ₹208 average bill and 7.2 bills per resident per month, the ₹5/₹10 rack is the lever on bill COUNT and on children's pocket-money spend — and it is what a 5-18 year-old cohort with no other shop actually buys.

skuLines.examples: Sunfeast Dark Fantasy Choco Fills, Britannia Treat Croissant/Choco, Parle Hide & Seek Fills
skuLines.notes: Chocolate filling blooms above ~30°C — a cold hill location is actually an advantage here. Highest aspirational pull with the 10-20 age band.

skuLines.examples: Cadbury Oreo, Parle Hide & Seek Black Bourbon, Sunfeast Bounce
skuLines.notes: Check for egg-free status on premium biscuit lines before listing — most are veg-marked, but not all imported/premium ones are.

skuLines.examples: Karachi Bakery Pista/Fruit Biscuits, Unibic Choco Chip & Butter Cookies, Bonn La Americana Gourmet, Cookieman
skuLines.seasonality: Festival and gifting lift (Oct-Dec, Baisakhi, Gurpurab)
skuLines.notes: The premium end of the category and the visitor/gifting slot — a campus that hosts parents, sangat and guests needs something above ₹150 to hand over. Long shelf life, no cold chain, high value density per truck-kg: an ideal hill-logistics SKU.

skuLines.examples: Britannia NutriChoice Digestive & Oats, Sunfeast Farmlite Digestive, McVitie's Digestive, Patanjali Digestive
skuLines.notes: Health-oriented biscuits (multigrain, high-fibre, low-sugar) are the fastest-growing biscuit sub-segment in India. For a campus with teaching staff and elderly residents this is a real must-have, not a premium indulgence.

skuLines.examples: Britannia NutriChoice Sugar Free, Sunfeast Farmlite Sugarless, Unibic Sugar Free, Karachi Sugar Free
skuLines.notes: Slow-moving but non-substitutable: a diabetic resident 30-50 km from a market has no alternative. Keep 2 SKUs, 1-2 facings, and accept the low turn — this is a service line, not a growth line.

skuLines.examples: Early Foods Ragi Jaggery Cookies, Slurrp Farm Millet Cookies, Timios, Milatos millet snacks, Sunfeast Farmlite Millet
skuLines.notes: Millet and jaggery-sweetened, maida-free cookies are the strongest 2026 innovation stream in Indian bakery and index high with young staff parents. Higher margin than mass biscuits; verify jaggery-not-sugar and eggless claims on pack.

skuLines.examples: RiteBite Max Protein 7 Grains Choco Chips Cookie, Yoga Bar cookies, Max Protein assorted 6-pack
skuLines.notes: Protein-enriched baked goods are forecast to keep growing into 2026, and the 18-25 university cohort with gym habits is exactly the buyer. 1-2 SKUs; the price point limits volume in a ₹208-average-bill store.

skuLines.examples: Early Foods Millet Teething Sticks & Rusks, Slurrp Farm Ragi Cookies, Timios organic multigrain cookies, Farex/Nestlé toddler biscuits
skuLines.notes: Married staff quarters with babies and small children are a stated resident group, and this is the one bakery need with no substitute at all — a parent will make a 30-50 km trip for it. Small, high-value, long shelf life: the cheapest possible line to carry and the most expensive one to be out of.

skuLines.line: Biscuit & cookie gift packs / assorted tins
skuLines.examples: Britannia Good Day gift pack, Sunfeast assorted, Karachi Bakery gift box, Milatos millet gift pack, Bonn gift assortment
skuLines.seasonality: Diwali/Oct-Nov, Christmas-New Year, Gurpurab, Baisakhi, and school parents'/visitors' days
skuLines.notes: Highest-value single unit in the category on q-commerce (gift packs up to ₹950). Buy to a hard window and a hard quantity — an unsold festival tin in February is dead stock. Non-alcoholic and eggless only for this campus.

skuLines.examples: Gloripan/Blue Bird instant yeast, Weikfield baking powder & cocoa, Morde choco chips & compound, icing sugar, vanilla essence
skuLines.seasonality: Birthday and festival clusters; winter home-baking
skuLines.notes: Q-commerce keeps 'Baking Ingredients' inside the Bakery & Biscuits category, and in a township with no cake shop nearby, staff families bake at home. Long shelf life, tiny space, good margin — an obvious gap-filler.

skuLines.examples: birthday candles, sprinkles/gems, edible icing tubes, cake boards & boxes, paper cake liners
skuLines.notes: Attaches directly to every cake sold — the cheapest incremental margin in the category. Non-perishable, so no risk. If the store sells a birthday cake and not a candle, the candle sale went 30-50 km away.

skuLines.examples: The Baker's Dozen Gluten Free, Wingreens/Health Kart GF loaf, jowar-bajra loaf
skuLines.notes: Genuinely tiny demand at 5,000 residents and a short shelf life at a high unit cost — carry only on named indent from a specific household, never on speculation.

trends2026: Sourdough is the No.1 talked-about bakery trend going into 2026 — consumer interest more than tripled in recent years and peaked in 2025; English Oven and The Baker's Dozen have both put retail sourdough loaves (₹145-235) on q-commerce shelves.
'Zero maida' / 100% atta claims have moved from premium niche to a mainstream shelf claim on bread and cookies (Britannia 'No Maida', The Baker's Dozen 'Zero Maida', RiteBite 'No Maida 7 Grains').

Millet and jaggery-sweetened baked goods are the biggest Indian innovation stream — millet, protein, fibre, low-sugar and clean-label are where bakery R&D budgets are going, and millet cookie brands (Early Foods, Slurrp Farm, Timios, Milatos) now hold real q-commerce shelf.

High-protein baked goods keep climbing — online conversation about protein-enriched bakery is forecast to grow another ~17% in 2026, and the fastest-growing buyer segment is children/teens as parents swap plain biscuits for protein-denser snacks.
Clean label / preservative-free is now a bakery purchase driver: no artificial colours or flavours, no palm oil, 'no added preservatives' (Bonn's La Americana Gourmet is a north-Indian example).

Q-commerce has exploded bakery assortment breadth — Blinkit's Bakery & Biscuits SKU count grew from ~1,250 to ~1,692 in a single month, with The Baker's Dozen (101 SKUs) out-listing Britannia (56). The reference set a shopper compares against is now far wider than a traditional store's.
Category price architecture has split hard: most bakery items still transact at ₹20-54, while the same category now carries ₹650-950 gift packs — a store needs both ends, and the middle is thinning.

Plum cake and festive cake have de-coupled from Christmas alone — vegan, sugar-free and alcohol-free variants have widened the buyer base across communities, and Dec-Jan can be 30-40% of a bakery's annual revenue.

Supermarket in-store bake-off counters (warm bread, custom cakes) have become a primary differentiator in Indian modern trade, where supermarkets/hypermarkets now hold ~35% of the Indian bakery market.
adjacentServices: Order-a-day-ahead eggless celebration cake book — take birthday/anniversary/farewell orders at the POS counter with a WhatsApp confirmation; ~5,000 residents implies 400+ birthdays a month and this is the single largest wallet currently leaking to a 30-50 km town trip.

In-house bake-off unit (par-baked or scratch) at the warehouse or a canteen kitchen — solves the 2-5 day bread shelf life that hill-road inbound cannot serve, and moves bread/pastry/patties from 8-15% branded MRP margin to 30-65% own-produced margin. Needs an FSSAI manufacturing/kitchen endorsement, not just the retail licence.
Standing hostel/canteen bread-and-rusk indent, priced and forecast separately from POS retail — an institutional flow at 6-12% margin should never be blended into shelf-offtake planning.
Hot savoury bakery counter at the canteens (veg patties, puff, kulcha, hot bread) on the Himachal hill-town bakery model — the cheapest footfall driver in a cold climate, at 45-65% margin.
Tea-time combo bundling — rusk/khari/dry-cake sold with chai at the canteens and Ary Lite, which is exactly how these products are consumed here anyway.

Loose-buy-and-repack line for khari, fan, dry cake and bakery cookies from a regional Solan/Nahan/Paonta Sahib baker — 30-50% margin versus 8-15% on branded packs, needs airtight tins plus clean FSSAI-compliant repacking and labelling.

Festival/gifting pre-book (Diwali, Christmas, Gurpurab, Baisakhi, parents' day) — take orders in advance on gift tins and festive cake so the seasonal buy is against confirmed demand and nothing is left as February dead stock.
Cake accessory attach at the till (candles, boards, boxes, sprinkles) — 25-40% margin, zero spoilage, and it captures the party spend the cake itself opens up.

Special-diet standing indent (diabetic/sugar-free biscuits, gluten-free bread, baby teething rusks) on a named-household basis rather than speculative shelf stock — a service promise for residents who have no alternative supplier.
